To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the domain of analyticity of a fixed transfer amplitude can be extended from |t|<t0 to |t|<4μ2, whereμ2 is the pion-pole residue, (2) the extension can be made in such a way that the extended domain is a natural one, (3) the extended domain contains part of the cut in thet-plane of the double spectral function, (4) this is a consequence of the fact that in the extended domain

(i) the domain of analyticity of the scattering amplitude is larger than the physical region of the s- and t-channel, (ii) it includes the Mandelstamm double spectral functions, and (iii) the domain of validity of the fixed energy dispersion relations is a region that includes the Mandelstmam double spectral function.

1) the fixed energy sections of scattering amplitude are in fact analytic in a region of the complex s-plane containing part of the Mandestram cuts and 2) the domain of analyticity of the absorptive parts of scattering amplitues contains part of the double-spectral function of Mandelstam.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the analyticity domain obtained is not a natural one, either from the pure analytic continuation point of view, or from the point of view of the elastic unitarity condition.
the fixed-energy sections of the amplitude are analytic for all values of the energy, but not necessarily the full amplitude.

we now have a very good understanding of the analytic structure of the scattering amplitudes for pion-pion, pion-kaon and kaon-kaon scattering, in the region of the Mandel-stam plane where the elastic unitarity condition is fulfilled.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown how to extend the domain of the pion-pi scattering amplitudes from the region of validity of the fixed t dispersion relations to the region of validity for the Mandelstamm double spectral function.
the analyticity domain for pion-pion amplitudes can be extended from the fixed t dispersion relation domain to the topological product domain |t|<4μ2×s, and further to a natural region in thet plane.
we have extended the axiomatic domain for the elastic pion-pion amplitude by the elastic unitarity condition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the domain of analyticity of the pion-particle scattering amplitude is larger than the domain predicted by Mandelstam’s analyticity theorem, and that this domain is not natural.

we can use the analytic structure of the amplitude to determine the analytic structure of its absorptive part, which is the main quantity we need to determine in order to extract the scattering amplitudes.
the Mandelstamm double spectral function is a natural object in the sense of the analyticity of the absorptive parts of the amplitudes, which is not true for the single spectral function.
